positions.summary: PCF programme (proposition 127) reinstates the wealth tax, triples its yield, raises its rates and progressivity, and abolishes the flat tax (PFU).
positions.nuance: The asset base is not spelled out, but the ISF being restored included financial assets, so a restored and tripled ISF meets the statement in full. The detailed text is the 2022 'Jours heureux' programme, which pcf.fr still shows as the platform in 2026. The 2027 campaign site (fabienroussel2027.fr) has no detailed programme yet.

positions.summary: The PCF is listed among the left-wing parties that back the Zucman tax. Its own programme goes further, with a tripled ISF.
positions.nuance: This is the party's position. No personal Roussel statement on the Zucman tax was verified (web search budget exhausted). Coded +2 because the party backs the measure outright, and the tripled-ISF programme goes beyond it.

positions.summary: The programme (proposition 11) abolishes the CICE-derived employer-contribution exemptions. A PCF petition calls for conditioning business aid and cutting the number of business tax breaks and subsidies by two thirds.
positions.nuance: Production taxes are not addressed explicitly. Roussel is friendly to SMEs and industry, but the programme removes existing contribution cuts rather than adding new ones.

positions.summary: The programme opposes free-trade treaties and calls for 'maîtrise des échanges' through a replacement for the WTO (proposition 171). Roussel campaigns on reindustrialisation.
positions.nuance: No explicit tariff or quota proposal, and no acceptance of higher prices, was found. Coded +1 as a partial match.

positions.summary: Proposes nationalising TotalEnergies and Engie alongside EDF. The programme lists nationalisations (EDF, Engie, SNCF and others), and Roussel calls for renationalising the motorways.
Proposition 128 makes inheritance tax much more progressive (twice as many brackets) and repeals avoidance schemes, with a EUR 170,000 allowance.
positions.nuance: Mixed in effect: the allowance would lower tax on modest estates, while large estates would pay more. Overall direction is against lowering the tax, hence -1.

positions.summary: Retirement at 60 on a full pension (proposition 8).
positions.nuance: Goes beyond 62.

positions.summary: Opposes any rise. Wants retirement at 60.
The PCF defends the pay-as-you-go system and opposes funded pensions.
positions.nuance: The programme pages opened do not mention capitalisation explicitly. This is the long-standing party line, not directly sourced this session.

positions.summary: The programme (proposition 156) wants to permanently end the 3% deficit rule and the stability pact, which it calls an 'austerity straitjacket'. It also recruits 500,000 public employees.
Proposes creating 500,000 public-service jobs (proposition 29).
A large public-service and investment programme, financed mainly through taxing capital and a democratically controlled ECB (proposition 157). No explicit statement on debt was verified.
positions.nuance: Coded +1 because the emphasis is on tax and ECB credit rather than debt as such.

positions.summary: The programme rejects the 3% deficit rule and the stability pact. A constitutional deficit cap runs directly against it.
positions.nuance: The constitutional golden rule is not addressed by name. The position is deduced from the explicit rejection of deficit caps.

positions.summary: Raise the SMIC quickly to 1,600 euros net (proposition 1).
The programme (proposition 2) restores the jobseeker rights cut by earlier governments, both the qualifying period and the benefit level.

As a deputy, Roussel voted against the whole projet de loi pour le plein emploi at first reading (10 Oct 2023). That law created the 15-20 hours of activity required of RSA recipients. No 2025-2026 promise to abolish the obligation was found.
positions.nuance: He opposed creating the obligation, but no abolition pledge was found, so this is -1 rather than -2. The PCF programme on pcf.fr (proposition 42) wants to open the RSA to under-25s and eventually replace it with a guaranteed job or training scheme.

positions.summary: 32-hour week with no loss of pay (proposition 9).

The programme opens legal, safe routes for migrants and expands refugee reception (proposition 162). Roussel says he does not link immigration to unemployment, though his 'frontières passoires' rhetoric is less liberal than the rest of the left.
positions.nuance: No statement on volumes of work, family or student immigration was found. Coded -1 rather than -2 because his rhetoric is more ambivalent than the programme.

Only limited European cooperation, for example on satellite positioning (geolocation), is accepted.
positions.nuance: The booklet accepts targeted European cooperation and wants a European defence industrial and technological base, but it rejects any loss of French military autonomy. It is a party document, not a Roussel interview.

record.bio: Fabien Roussel (born 16 April 1969 in Béthune) is a former journalist who became national secretary of the Parti communiste français (PCF) on 25 November 2018. He was deputy for Nord's 20th constituency from June 2017 to June 2024 and the PCF's 2022 presidential candidate (2.28%, 8th place). He has been mayor of Saint-Amand-les-Eaux since 30 January 2025 and was re-elected in March 2026. According to French Wikipedia (citing Le Figaro), he announced his 2027 presidential candidacy on TF1 on 6 September 2026 under the slogan "Vivre".
offices: National secretary (secrétaire national) of the PCF
legal: Mediapart (2022) alleged that Roussel held a fictitious job as parliamentary assistant to PCF deputy Jean-Jacques Candelier (2009-2014). The Parquet national financier opened a preliminary investigation on 11 March 2022. Roussel denies the allegation and says he worked on following conflicts in the Douaisis; Candelier told L'Humanité that Roussel did work as his assistant. No charge (mise en examen) or closure is reported; status taken from French Wikipedia, not confirmed against a court or AFP source.

reversals.before: Advocated France leaving NATO's integrated command, presented as necessary for national independence.
reversals.after: After Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, he no longer proposes French withdrawal from NATO (he still opposes Ukraine joining NATO and the EU).

delivery.what: Deputy 2017-2024 in opposition (PCF / GDR group). He was rapporteur of a bill to create a French list of tax havens (2017-2018). No law adopted under his name is documented in the sources consulted.
delivery.assessment: Legislative record could not be checked against roll-call sites (datan.fr, nosdeputes.fr) or cross-lean outlets; only a secondary source (Wikipedia) was available.

delivery.what: 2022 presidential programme proposals (not enacted): SMIC raised to 1,500 euros net, legal retirement age back to 60, wealth tax restored and tripled, recruitment of 30,000 police, and an energy mix of nuclear and renewables.
delivery.assessment: These are campaign proposals, not delivered measures; the 2027 programme was not verified.

delivery.what: Mayor of Saint-Amand-les-Eaux since 30 January 2025, succeeding Alain Bocquet; his list won the March 2026 municipal election in the first round with 51.06% and he was re-elected mayor on 22 March 2026.
delivery.assessment: Executive record is short (about 1.7 years); no assessment of his municipal record was found in the sources consulted.

media_portrayal.left_media: Not verified directly. Mediapart published the 2022 fictitious-job allegation; Roussel responded by accusing its founder Edwy Plenel of publishing it to favour Mélenchon's candidacy.
media_portrayal.right_media: Not verified directly. Wikipedia records a March 2025 CNews appearance in which he said anti-white racism exists; how right-leaning outlets frame him could not be checked.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Not verified directly; Le Monde, franceinfo, AFP and Public Sénat coverage could not be fetched.
